string.text: Document
Conclusion on a genetic engineering project
Access card
Access card to the control system of the main module of the emitter.
Notes of an unknown stalker

This crumpled pile of incomprehensible documents and newspaper clippings clearly intrigued its owner. Tucked among them is a school notebook, filled with jaggy handwriting of an unknown author. 
The writing is riddled with errors, constantly changes topics, and presents a conspiracy theory about a certain group of scientists who allegedly developed psychotronic weapons back in the USSR and are now using them to rule the world. 
The author believes that these scientists, who in their view are simultaneously humanists, idealists, and self-serving eminences grises, have accidentally created the Zone. And to this day, they allegedly continue to work in the depths of the fourth unit of the Chernobyl NPP, enforcing their will upon the rulers of states. 
This pile of waste paper may be of interest to some traders.
"Z-ITCh-12" Device
An unknown device with the inscription “Z-ITCh-12” on the rim. \nLooks broken, but may be of interest to some scientists.
"Anti-Emission" Prototype
A prototype of special equipment. In theory, it is capable of protecting the carrier from the lethal effects of the emissions. \nService life of the device is very limited.
Measuring device

A prototype of special equipment that measures anomalous activity during the active phase of the emission. \nTo activate, deploy the device in the open field during the intermediate phase of the emission.
Log from underground chambers

A log found in the underground chambers under the site adjacent to the “Rostok” factory, which contains data on shipments of certain “biomaterials” for unknown purposes. \nMay be of interest to Snitch.
Report on the emitter tests
Report on the emitter tests

The folder contains a detailed report on the impact of elevated radiation levels on the psyche of the inhabitants of the contaminated areas, as well as a document titled “Report on the Tests of the Psychoemotional Correction Emitter”: 
“1. The tests conducted on animals and human subjects, specifically the ones placed in an induced coma or the ones with cognitive disabilities were successful. Full control over the subjects was achieved. 
2. Tests on healthy human subjects were less successful. However, we’ve managed to moderately affect the subjects’ consciousness and indoctrinate them with simple programs, which they’ve successfully executed. 
3. Increasing the power may lead to negative side effects, notably: increased aggression and an inability to follow the commands specified by the programs. 
4. The introduction of a low power emitter in the NPP personnel’s town has positively affected their working capacity and alertness, while also alleviating the emotional tension among the subjects.”
The CNPP research team’s documents

These documents belonged to a research team and contain data from all kinds of measurements and a briefing sheet: \n”At Colonel's request, I'm writing down the further plan of action 'so you, stupid eggheads, don't get lost': we will enter the Sarcophagus from the northern side, then pass through the turbine hall to the reactor, where, according to the data, the source of psi-emission is located. After taking the measurements, we must notify Colonel as the team leader and thereafter follow his instructions without question. \nJust need to make sure we finish up before the emission.”
Report from the "Rostok" Factory
Report from the "Rostok" Factory

It appears that this document was stored in less-than-ideal conditions; the ink has blurred, rendering large parts of the text undecipherable: \n“…which led to a conflict between the group responsible for developing the psychotronic suppression emitter and the heads of the “Project Cover”. The final straw was one of the project head’s reports, which unequivocally hinted at subjecting the scientific staff to effects of the low-power mobile emitters in order to improve their work capacity and maintain high morale within the team. Shortly after that, following actions were taken in order to…”
Order from the "Rostok" Factory
Order from the "Rostok" Factory

It appears that this document was stored in less-than-ideal conditions; the ink has blurred, rendering large parts of the text undecipherable: 
 "ORDER 
on the installation and equipment start-up in the Pripyat area

 In order to ensure that the work schedule (from 21:00 to 23:00) is…"
Diary of Journalist
Diary of Journalist

In addition to Middleman’s personal documents, the folder contains a notebook page that seems to have been torn out of the diary of the legendary stalker Journalist: 
 “Gunslinger says he no longer trusts the scientists from Yantar. Something changed in him after the trip to the Center. He talked about the strange things that happen there and suggested we go together next time. I agreed — someone needs to watch his back now that he was wounded. 
 But first we need to visit the Dark Valley. Snitch reported that there was something interesting for us there.’‘

 ‘‘This raid into the Valley was almost our last. My intuition tells me - it was a trap. The military were waiting for us at the exit of the complex. Without Gunslinger’s help I wouldn’t have survived that rendezvous. 
 We found what we were searching for, but there was no information on the Monolith there. Yes, the International Research Center was conducting some dubious genetic research there, but that’s of no interest to us. 
 It seems I have no choice; I’ll have to turn to the eggheads from Yantar. Maybe they have some info. 
 And then, I’ll head North. I’ve become just like Gunslinger. I don’t trust anyone.”
Mope's PDA

The owner of this PDA had a habit of recording his thoughts on a voice recorder, but only the last entry is of interest: \n”I seized the container from Middleman. He forced me to do it the hard way. Ah, whatever, what’s done is done… I just realized that the container is not so simple. It’s locked with a code. Damn, I need to… I need to go back… I need to go back to the meeting place and… maybe I’ll find a way to open it. And then… then it’ll just be a case for small.”
Note from Mope to Sanya Hog
Memo from Mope to Middleman

Middleman, I'm looking for Journalist. I have what he's looking for. I hear you know how to find him. I'll be waiting in the apartment building, the one on the south side, opposite the school. Come alone. \nMesser.
Damaged PDA from Dark Valley
Damaged PDA from Dark Valley

Amidst the array of corrupted, unreadable data, an almost intact message stands out: \n”And one more thing. The lab has an exit t%4K;=/)9JK*-;NJ(N21owever, according to some reports, the entrance there is locked from the inside. Check it out, if possible, but prioritize taking the measurements above all.”
Pursuer's PDA

The owner of this PDA didn't bother with scouring his emails or maintaining secrecy. Among the many irrelevant senders, the owner of the “Stalker” bar, Rat, stands out: “He's heading North. Track his route to the Center, but don't bother going to Pripyat—it's a deathtrap. If he wants to pass through the city, then to hell with him; the military will finish him off.”
PDA of a military stalker callsigned “Blue 9”
This PDA is locked. Some expert assistance is required to hack it.

Extracted emails from the hacked PDA of the military stalker callsigned “Blue 9”: 
 “The subject has discovered fragments 1 and 3. Moving out now to sector 28.” 
 “To units “White” and “Green”: Sector 26 has been assigned as the extraction point.” 
 “To unit “Blue”: Three samples of anomalous formations #24 have been found at Cordon: near the boiler-house; near the water tower; near the destroyed building in the village.” 
 “To all units: a reserve weapons cache has been prepared in the Red Forest; the geo-tag is attached to the message. Use only in case of emergency.” 
 “Note to self: contact Major about the subject.”
Note from the “Rostok” factory’s manager
“Rostok” factory manager's note

A typewritten sheet of paper with a marginal note: “The access code to the airlock is 2565.” 
”Deliver in person. 
To the Director of the “Rostok” factory, M.V. Petrov. 

 As per your instructions, access from the factory's premises to the special zone has been restricted; the installation of the armored door has been completed. The following have been sent to the lower levels of the workshops: a batch of gas masks and work clothes—140 sets; marked boxes—3 pcs. 
 Meanwhile, I highly anticipate a personal meeting with you. Although you asked me not to question your decisions, I still believe I should be informed of the destination of the incoming train cars. They are clearly coming from the city via the route under the lake, but why such secrecy? 
 Please understand that my job requires me to be prepared for the unexpected; I would much prefer to not jeopardize my career over this matter. 
Sincerely, 
Operations Manager of the “Rostok” Factory 
Mikhalchuk S.P.”
Gravi-hammer
A gravitational sledgehammer, most likely created by the Burers. Snitch asked me to keep it safe and sound.
“Psi-mark” scanner
An experimental prototype capable of detecting the contamination of biological material by the psi-emission. \nTo activate, aim the device at the target and initiate a scan.
Journalist’s notes on “Sin” base
Journalist’s notes on “Sin” base

Damn, how did I get myself into such a mess. I shouldn't have gone to the base of those “gray brothers” lunatics. Well, at least they didn't take my notebook and pen, and they do feed me. But why are they even doing that? \nWell, it doesn't really matter. What matters is that the “Winds of Madness” must be somewhere close. \nBut first, I need to get out. My chance will definitely come and I won’t miss it.
Access card
Personal access card of a research group staff member.
Psi-Stabilizer
An experimental prototype that protects the wearer from the fatal effects of the apparitions. Ineffective against other forms of psi-emissions.
Sporecatcher
A device that captures and collects the parasite’s spores for subsequent analysis. \nTo activate, place the device near the source of the spores.
Ramblings of an unknown stalker

The unknown owner has preserved this folder as best as he could; the paper inside is almost as good as new. Among the many incomprehensible and illiterate entries, the meaning of which is likely only known to the author, one catches the eye with some familiar words: 
“Scienters. They are to blame for everything. The four main ones are now in an induced coma, and if I'm not mistaken, and I am not, they control not only everything. The Zone, the City, the not-Zone, the not-City—they control everything. 
No, I can't be fooled. I understand everything. I'm not a fool, not a simpleton, not a scienter, not a soldier, not a fanatic, not a journalist, not a doctor, not a gunslinger. 
But He knows the code. He wrote it down, wrote it down precisely. And hid it securely in a hiding place. Rostok. That’s where I saw it, underground. Just like in the dream, but in reality.”
Documentation: “Psi-stabilizer”

A thick folder titled: “Documentation for a protection device to be used in conditions of elevated background psi-emission.” \nSurprisingly, all the pages remained intact. In the margins of the reports, neatly and evenly written notes were made in pencil, persistently pushing for the reduction of power consumption of the primary unit which would allow to improve the device's mobility.
Documentation: “Psi-locator”

A worn-down folder titled “Documentation for the Scanner of the Bioelectrical Activity of the Brains of Psionic Mutants.” \nFrom reading the surviving pages, it can be concluded that the scanner is capable of locating psionic mutants based on the unique rhythm of their brain activity.
Documentation: "Anti-radiation suit”

An old, yellowed folder titled “Documentation for the Radiation-Protection Suit.” 
Inside, in addition to the suit's schematics, are instructions for its use and some documents from the supplier “the Radiation Safety Research Institute”. 
According to the documents, the suit features a closed-cycle respiratory system and a new-generation insulating coating, which partially stops the flow of hot particles. However, the safety tests have revealed certain issues with the suit's mobility and resistance to mechanical damage. 
The need for further work to eliminate the identified issues of the prototype, as well as the need to conduct additional testing, were noted.
Documentation: "Military-grade software"

A recently printed folder titled “Documentation for Experimental Military-grade Software for Expeditionary Units.” \nInside is documentation for specialized software installed onto the PDAs of military stalker expeditionary units. This software scans the area within a 50-meter radius around the user for the presence of the PDA signals. \nThen, based on the information obtained from the scanned PDA, as well as the messages about the owner from the stalker network, the software determines the owner's faction affiliation, reputation in the stalker community, and the expected attitude toward the user, and forms a short dossier.
Cargo for Professor Gorbovsky
A hefty container with unknown contents.
Zombified stalker’s PDA

The data on this PDA is severely damaged; only the last entry is partially readable: “/n0xF9A%/#A's accumulator is almost out of charge; I think this is the last entry. I don't know how many days I've been stuck here, and I don't know how to get out, but I can hear sounds! As if people are walking behind the wall. I kept shouting at them till my voice gave out, but it was no use; either they couldn't hear me, or they were ignoring me. And before that I heard that guy from the death truck slipping me something. I’m here because of him! Oh well, once I get out, I'll tell everything. About him, and about that Major... they thought I didn't know, haha. You will get your dues! All of you! I just need to get out before the food runs out. Gunslinger said, that in ord;’^%\F?+/C6”
Documentation on “C-Consciousness Project”

An old, yellowed folder, some of the pages inside crumble at the slightest touch, others are barely legible. 
From what’s been read, it can be concluded that the primary goal of the “C-Consciousness Project” was to create a unified consciousness capable of exerting psychotronic influence on those around it. 
Subsequently, it was intended to use this “C-Consciousness” to influence various political authorities, the masses, and certain individuals. 
How the scientists planned to control this “C-Consciousness” is not specified; perhaps that information has been lost along with the pages that crumbled into dust.
Documentation on controllers

An old, yellowed folder, soaked with moisture. From the surviving pages, it can be concluded that this folder contains data on experiments that have created the psionic mutants known as controllers. 
Without the help of a geneticist it’s hardly possible to tell head or tails of what these experiments were exactly, but one thing is certain: the controllers are the result of human experimentation. 

Excerpt from the documents: 
 “These mutants are tall, have an asthenic build, arachnodactyly of the hands and feet, funnel-shaped or keeled chest deformity, and kyphoscoliosis. 
 A genetically determined disorder of the metabolism of the sulfur-containing amino acid methionine (GCM) is caused by a block in the enzyme ?-cystathionine synthase. Homocystinuria (HCU) is characterized by focal neurological symptoms, ectopia lentis, skeletal deformities, thromboembolism, and cardiovascular disease. The HCU gene is mapped to the long arm of chromosome 21 (21q21-q22.1). Homozygosity for the 677C-T mutation in the 5,10-methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) locus, a folate-dependent enzyme important in homocysteine metabolism, can render the enzyme heat-labile and less active and is associated with elevated plasma total homocysteine levels.”
Note from the lab under the Generators

A strange note, the author of which seemingly tried to resist the force controlling him. 
”You are the one who will stop them. They control you, but as you write this, as you read this, you are... it doesn't matter what your name is, it doesn't matter if you can remember what you’re called, what matters is that you are the one who will stop them. 
All you have to do is pull the switches. Five bodies, five switches, five little jobs to do. Four are asleep, one is awake, but he has other things to worry about besides you.
Pull yourself together and remember. You are the one who will stop them. 

And I am The One Who Controls You.”
Professor Gorbovsky’s suicide note

Messer, I’m sorry. I've remembered everything. I dedicated my entire life to science, I believed in progress and its benefit to humanity, I set great goals for myself, but now I can see the consequences of my actions. 
I'm sorry You are left to live in this "brave new world" we’ve created. I can't fix my mistakes, but I can help you. I’ve left some notes on the documents about the "Winds of Madness"; I'm sure they'll be useful to you. 
Please forgive me for my actions, but I can no longer live peacefully with myself. 
Go North, Messer, there you will find all the answers. 
Gorbovsky
Documents on the “Winds of Madness” with a note

There was clearly an attempt to destroy these documents; traces of soot are visible on the cover, and the corners of the pages are blackened. 
The cover now contains a note from Professor Gorbovsky: “Thanks to these papers, I was able to calculate the exact cooling time for the emitter — from 9:00 PM to 11:00 PM. During the cooling phase, the emitter operates at low power, so you will still need proper psi-protection. Once you make your way to the maintenance lab, you’ll be able to disable it. Good luck.” 
The folder contains technical documents for a certain “Kaymanov emitter” and a draft of the letter addressed to a certain V. M. Chubko.

”I’ve attended the testing of the Kaymanov emitter today. Not only were the drugs not distributed properly, but the “biological material” were wandering around the complex completely unguarded! An utter disregard for safety regulations! 
 And the emitter itself is completely useless; not only the equipment and cooling system costs are astronomical, it also requires a whole NPP to be nearby to operate! So, mobility is out of the question, and if the interlock system overheats the entire device will spiral out of control and begin brainwashing everyone in the vicinity indiscriminately! 
 I'm already studying the blueprints (don't ask me how I got them; you won't believe it). I'll send them to you along with this letter so you can see for yourself.
 If you want a reliable solution to the foreign elements for security of the Central Lab, use our unit instead.
 However, the choice is yours. If you want to have a problematic emitter right next to you, go ahead, Vadim Mikhailovich, but I will not be responsible for the consequences. Next time, I'll file an official complaint to the Group for review.
Prikhodko P.S.”
A PDA containing information on the location of a cache with documents on the “Psi-helmet” device.
Documentation: “Psi-helmet”

An unremarkable-looking folder, but its contents are quite remarkable. Inside are laminated sheets with instructions for assembling the “Psi helmet” device, as well as associated documentation. Each page is meticulously arranged, ensuring it can be understood by a knowledgeable specialist. \nAccording to the numerous notes and attached experimental results, assembling such a device would require some rare and difficult-to-manufacture components, as well as certain degree of knowledgeability of neurobiology and cybernetics to precisely tune it to the specifics of the source of psi-emission.
Crate with medical supplies
A crate marked with an emblem of the “Duty” faction.
Documents on the “Winds of Madness”

There was clearly an attempt to destroy these documents; traces of soot are visible on the cover, and the corners of the pages are blackened. The folder contains technical documents for a certain “Kaymanov emitter” and a draft of the letter addressed to a certain V. M. Chubko.

”I’ve attended the testing of the Kaymanov emitter today. Not only were the drugs not distributed properly, but the “biological material” were wandering around the complex completely unguarded! An utter disregard for safety regulations! 
 And the emitter itself is completely useless; not only the equipment and cooling system costs are astronomical, it also requires a whole NPP to be nearby to operate! So, mobility is out of the question, and if the interlock system overheats the entire device will spiral out of control and begin brainwashing everyone in the vicinity indiscriminately! 
 I'm already studying the blueprints (don't ask me how I got them; you won't believe it). I'll send them to you along with this letter so you can see for yourself.
 If you want a reliable solution to the foreign elements for security of the Central Lab, use our unit instead.
 However, the choice is yours. If you want to have a problematic emitter right next to you, go ahead, Vadim Mikhailovich, but I will not be responsible for the consequences. Next time, I'll file an official complaint to the Group for review.
Prikhodko P.S.”
Key to the safe of “Sin”
The key to the safe at the “Sin” faction's base.
Protective boots
Boots made of a special material that can protect the wearer from the aggressive acidic environment of Lake Yantar.
Hoplite's PDA
This PDA is locked. Some expert assistance is required to hack it.

Among the irrelevant correspondence, personal notes, and bunch of fantasy books, there's one notable entry: 
 “The day before yesterday, I’ve ran into Journalist near the swamp. I had to drag him back to my hut to get him back on his feet. The artifact I was saving for Toad had to be used for that, but it is what it is. Gotta stay out of trouble till I find a replacement. 
 As Journalist began to recover, he mentioned that he was being pursued, but didn't say by whom. 
 Today we bid our farewells — he's headed somewhere North, maybe planning to meet his informants there. 
 Before leaving, he asked if I'd been to the archives of the local research institute. He was interested in some papers about equipment deliveries to a lab in the Red Forest. 
 If I’m in the area — I'll look for it, then pass it on to Journalist whenever we meet again."
Diary of an unknown stalker

Someone's diary. The entries are undated and barely legible, the author's handwriting is messy, and the spelling leaves much to be desired. 
According to the first entries, the author hid some important materials in the city of Bright Beam — in a briefcase under the bathtub, then set off for the “Rostok” factory through the city's catacombs and got lost. By paths unknown to himself, he traversed territories blocked by the psi-emissions of the "Winds of Madness". 
The last entry reads: 
 “I’ve managed on my own. On my own! Without scienters, without the military, without gunslingers, and without journalists. And I don't need any doctors either, and I don't need any treatment! 
 I've walked paths they never dreamed of; the Zone itself led me! 
This here is their lair, from there they rule the Zone, and rule the not-Zone, and rule everything! But they won't be able to keep calling themselves the kings of the world for long. The end is near! The Zone will be free!”
Diary of stalker Buffalo
Diary of stalker Buffalo

Most of the pages are blurred due to a contact with decomposing corpse, but some of the entries are legible. 
”April 2, 2012, 6:23 PM. Signed up for an expedition to the city; was promised an NDP suit as a reward. It's high time to trade in my old suit for something better. 
April 3, 2012, 12:07 PM. Made it to the Freedom base. Only Chrome and a few of his guys were there. He warned me that the zombies go wild before the blowout, and it's best to hide somewhere an hour or two before. Well, I'll keep that in mind. 
April 3, 2012, 11:40 PM. Finally found that fucking flat the egghead was talking about. I’ve replaced the battery, so might as well spend the night here. The door switch works, so the apartment should be safe. 
April 4, 2012, 03:14 AM. The noise woke me up, it’s the fucking zombies banging on the door. Hopefully, they’ll get tired of it and fuck away by the morning. 
April 4, 2012, 08:45 AM. They didn't leave, the fuckers can sense me. Fucking hell, what am I supposed to do now? PDA is dead, so I can't even call for help. And I was gonna buy a spare accumulator. 
April 4, 2012, ... Yeah, that was a bad fucking idea. I tried to open the door, but fat fucking chance, one of the rotters even managed to bite through my suit. 
April 4, 2012, ... The wound is covered in white foam, fuck. 
April 4, 2012, ... It's getting dark. Just this blinking fucking light bulb and the howling of the zombies. The wound hurts, it's covered in ulcers. Why did I ever sign up for this? 
April 5, 2012, … It's dawn. The door won't budge at all, but at least the brainless fucks have stopped the pounding. They’re just standing there, and muttering some nonsense. My head is buzzing, there's a ringing in my ears, I’m freezing. Infection? 
April _, 2012, … I’ve kept shouting out the window till my voice went hoarse, tried firing some shots up the sky, but no one answered. 
___ _,____, … The ringing in my ears isn't due to infection. The brain-fucker is hiding somewhere nearby. I heard him in my head, talking some dumb shit. That's why the brainless fucks are crowding there, he ordered them to. 
I don't know why the fuck he’s been playing with me, but I’ve had enough. If anyone finds my fucking body, take whatever you want. And tell that old fuck Gorbovsky to fuck himself. 
Stalker Buffalo”
Brain wave frequency imitator
An experimental device that protects the wearer from the powerful psi-emission of the psionic mutants by imitating the brain wave frequency of the zombified.
Decoy
An experimental device capable of luring out a rare mutant living in the swamps of the city of Bright Beam. \nTo activate, place the device in the designated area.
Package for Ferret
A box of ammunition that must be given to Ferret.
Ferret's backpack
A heavy backpack with unknown content that must be delivered to Toad.
Diary of stalker Navidson

An old, blood-soaked diary found in the cabin of a diesel locomotive. The cover is signed “The Navidson Record”.\n The blood has washed away the ink; only the last entry is fully legible. Judging by its absurd content, the author tried to hide from the blowout, but it was already too late.\n “The voices still swirl in the maze of the cavities of my skull. They don't want to come out. They ask me to look out the window, to see what's left. There's Nothing there. Nothing. But I drown them out, because I'll lose my mind if I look out. There's the Void out there. No colour and no space. Who will remain in their right mind when they see the Void? No one. There's nothing there. There's only the house inside of me, and I'm inside that house. The endless house older than the time itself. And on the outside, there's nothing. Pure nothingness. The Void. Sometimes I hear something creaking or growling on the other side. It's all in my head, all in my head. There's nothing out there. I crawl around the house, because God forbid, I might see the Void. My body aches. My head, too. The dosimeter kept crackling; I fed it to the Void so it wouldn't distract me. And now I'm completely alone. Just my Self and the Void.”
Correspondence from Lake Yantar
Correspondence from Lake Yantar

TOP SECRET 
To the Head of the “Barrier” Project, 
D.Sc., Professor V.M. Chubko. 

 Report on the tests of the “ZX-16” emitter. 
 The tests were conducted in the “Perimeter Protection” mode under deliberate emergency conditions, which caused the “ZX-16” emitter to overheat. 
 During the tests, uncontrolled bursts of psi-emission were detected, at its peak it exceeded the calculated parameters of the emitter by 60%, which contradicts Kasyanov’s theory of “overheating of the emitter leads to a decrease in power”. 
 We assume that overheating causes an increase in the parameters of neural activity of the “I-1M”, turning the pseudomesocephalum from the source of the psi-emission into a repeater. 
 These unforeseen consequences of the tests allow us to assume that the combination of the emitter and the “I-1M” may provide a more reliable option for the operation of the “Psi-barrier system” than the “Rainbow-1”. 
 I would also like to inform you that the biomaterials became unusable as a result of these tests, therefore new shipments are required. 

To the Head of the ZX-16 Laboratory
PhD in Tech Prikhodko P.S.

 Pavel Stepanovich, these “unforeseen consequences” of yours from the unauthorized tests led to the loss of the biomaterial we acquired with great difficulty. Do you understand the gravity of your actions? 
 Please refrain from conducting further tests without my permission. I understand your eagerness to outdo your competitors, but don't lose your head. 
 Speaking of competitors, yesterday they achieved stable operation of their “psychoemotional correctors” with only a single shutdown for cooling off period per day. Your operating model (5 minutes on, 3 minutes off) is incomparable. 
 However, I do not wish to discourage you. I believe that this “brain” of yours is the future. But! We need the “Psi-barrier” in the present, so we plan to use a completely technological solution from your colleagues at “Rainbow-1” for now. 
 Continue your research at a moderate pace; you will be notified of new deliveries of biomaterials shortly.
PDA with documentation from Lake Yantar

A PDA belonging to an employee of the underground complex beneath Lake Yantar. It contains scans of the documents on the commencement of work on an “artificially grown biological psi-emitter”. \nAmong the files are data on the supply of biomaterials—feral dogs and wild wolves. The reports, addressed to a certain V.M. Chubko, state that these biomaterials are insufficient for long-term research. In response, an order to search for an alternative source of biomaterials was sent. \nAlso stored in the device's memory are instructions prescribed by the management, a group photo of the complex's employees celebrating New Year's in the laboratory, and a list of members of the first six-month research shift.
PDA with an evacuation order from Lake Yantar

PDA of an employee of the underground complex under Lake Yantar. An email marked “URGENT” was sent to its inbox: 
 “Due to the state of emergency, you are ordered to immediately: 
 1. Collect four sets of documentation containing reports on the laboratory's activities. Thereafter, destroy the original documents marked “Top Secret”. 
 2. Dispose of all the biomaterials. 
 3. Prepare the experimental program “Veil” for uploading into the pseudomesocephalum “I-1M”. 
 4. Set the laboratory into the power-saving mode and activate the backup power sources. 
 5. Activate all external tracking sensors. 
 6. Form four groups in accordance with the emergency instructions. Each group will receive a set of personal protective equipment and a set of documentation. 
 7. Seal off the laboratory.
 8. Move to the main laboratory in area Z17. 

Head of Laboratory “ZX-16”
PhD in Tech Prikhodko P.S.”
PDA of the head of the Lake Yantar lab

All data on this PDA has been erased, except for one text file titled “Last Will”: 
 “I humbly ask the finder to forward this letter to my colleagues, to whom I remained loyal till the very end. 
 Colleagues, please notify my loved ones and forward them the letter from my office at the Center. Thank you. 

 I am Pavel Stepanovich Prikhodko, head of the ZX-16 laboratory. 
 Two weeks ago, I’ve ordered the lab to be sealed off. After the disaster, contact with the Center was lost, continuing the work was impossible. 
 I’ve sent four groups with the priceless results of our endeavors to the Center, at least one of them should reach it. 
 I’ve stayed behind to upload the “Veil” program into the “I-1M”, which was supposed to instill absolute invisibility and a subconscious reluctance to approach the lab to everyone within a 300-meter radius.
 I don't know why, but the “Perimeter Defense” program has activated instead. Now, whenever I try to leave the lab, I pass out and awaken in the shielded room.
 I’ve spent two weeks here, trying to turn off the “brain” and figure out how could it even activate this program? The answer terrifies me. Perhaps my colleagues' most fantastic hypothesis about the self-learning capabilities of “I-1M” was correct. If so, that Monster is probably delighted by my torment.
 I’ve tried to kill it, but it was useless; the hull is protected by armored glass. The emitter can only be shut down from the backup control panel. I've trapped myself. 
 I’ve ran out of food and water, and the psi-emission will eventually destroy me as a person, leaving me a brain-dead shell for the few remaining days. I don't want that. So, I kept the last bullet for myself.
 Farewell, please don't think badly of me.”
PDA from the military helicopter
